proof:
# A parity-conditioned midpoint transport with exact density and cap bounds

Let C be a convex body in R^n x R^d with d>=1, and assume its positive
integer fibers K_z have positive total d-volume M. Write a_z=|K_z| and
mu=sum_z 1_(K_z) dx. Fibers of zero d-volume do not affect this note.
For each represented parity class r in (Z/2Z)^n, set

    I_r={z:a_z>0, z mod 2=r}, M_r=sum_(z in I_r) a_z.

There are p<=2^n represented classes. There exist finite measures eta_r,
supported on S=C intersect (Z^n x R^d), such that

  eta_r(S)=M_r,                    eta_r<=mu,
  integral (z,x) d eta_r = integral (z,x) d mu_r,
  eta_r(H)<=2 mu_r(H)             for every closed ambient halfspace H,
                                                               (1)

where mu_r is the restriction of mu to I_r. Consequently eta=sum_r eta_r
has the same total mass and centroid as mu and satisfies

    eta<=p mu<=2^n mu,        eta(H)<=2mu(H).           (2)

The first inequality is a density domination; the second simultaneously
controls every closed oblique or vertical halfspace. No depth guarantee
or indefinite iteration with a fixed density constant is asserted.

## 1. Pairwise bounded-density midpoint coupling

For positive-volume compact convex A,B of volumes a,b, there is a
probability coupling pi of their uniform laws such that the midpoint
probability law has density at most 1/sqrt(ab).

This is the same triangular Gaussian construction used in
`candidate 71bcdfc8eb8340c6`. For smoothed
uniform densities f<=1/a and g<=1/b, its triangular transport T has
positive diagonal derivatives and det DT=f/(g composed with T). The
midpoint map F=(Id+T)/2 has

    det DF>=sqrt(det DT).

Its pushforward density is at most sqrt(f(x)g(T(x)))<=1/sqrt(ab).
Weak compactness of the couplings, the continuous midpoint map, and
nonnegative continuous test functions pass this density bound to the
original compact bodies. The marginals retain their exact original
first moments. The output is supported in (A+B)/2. The construction
also includes A=B, when one may simply use the diagonal coupling.

## 2. The parity law and its fiberwise domination

Fix r. Choose an ORDERED pair of base indices z,w independently with
probabilities a_z/M_r and a_w/M_r, and conditional on these indices use
one of the pairwise couplings above. Give the resulting joint law total
mass M_r, then take the ambient midpoint

    ((z,x),(w,y)) -> ((z+w)/2,(x+y)/2).

The base midpoint is integral because z,w have the same parity.
Convexity puts the output in C. Both full ambient marginals of the joint
measure are exactly mu_r, so total mass and first moments in (1) follow.
The elementary closed-halfspace indicator inequality at a midpoint gives
eta_r(H)<=2mu_r(H), including all boundary mass.

Fix an output base k. The pair (z,w) contributes mass a_z a_w/M_r and
has continuous midpoint density at most 1/sqrt(a_z a_w). Thus the output
density at k is bounded by

  (1/M_r) sum_(z,w in I_r, z+w=2k) sqrt(a_z a_w)
    <= (1/M_r)
       sqrt[(sum_(z:2k-z in I_r) a_z)
            (sum_(z:2k-z in I_r) a_(2k-z))]
    <=1.                                                   (3)

The first inequality is Cauchy-Schwarz, and the reflected indexing in
the two sums is a bijection. Each output density is supported inside
K_k. Therefore eta_r<=mu, proving all of (1) and (2).

## 3. Exact decrease of integer-coordinate variance

Write bar_z_r=M_r^(-1)sum_(z in I_r)a_z z. Independence of the two base
indices gives, for every Euclidean quadratic form |.|^2,

 integral |z-bar_z_r|^2 d eta_r
       =(1/2) integral |z-bar_z_r|^2 d mu_r.             (4)

Consequently, if bar_z is the global integer-coordinate mean,

 integral |z-bar_z|^2 d eta
   =integral |z-bar_z|^2 d mu
        -(1/2)sum_r integral |z-bar_z_r|^2 d mu_r.       (5)

This is a strict decrease whenever some parity class contains two
distinct positive base indices. Continuous-coordinate variance is not
claimed to obey (4), since its pairwise couplings need not be independent.

## 4. Limits of the statement

Although eta_r<=mu for each separate class, their densities can overlap
at the same output fiber. Only eta<=p mu is justified. Applying the
construction afresh to a density bounded by p instead of by one can
multiply the constant; equations (1)-(5) do not yield a density-preserving
iterated contraction to at most 2^n fibers or to the centroid fiber.
The target remains a mixed measure, so invoking a sharp depth theorem
for it would be an additional, presently unproved step.

## 5. Sharpness of the density coefficient

For C=[0,2]^n x K, with |K|=a>0, all 3^n integer fibers equal K.
A parity class with s even coordinates has 2^s base points and mass 2^s a.
Under its independent base pair, the probability of midpoint
k=(1,...,1) is 2^(-s). Its output mass at that fiber is therefore exactly a.
Since eta_r<=1_K dx there, the output measure in that fiber equals
1_K dx. Summing all 2^n parity classes gives output density exactly 2^n
at k. Thus the coefficient 2^n in (2) cannot be improved for this precise
independent-base construction.

The coefficient 2 in the separate class cap bound is also sharp in
limits: for a class with base indices 0 and 2 and masses A and b,
a vertical cap z>=1 has input mass b and output mass
(2Ab+b^2)/(A+b), whose ratio to b tends to 2 as b/A tends to zero.
Such endpoint volumes are compatible with an interpolating positive
middle fiber; that extra parity class is not part of this separate-class
sharpness assertion.
